```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

In `2025-11-06` `bpp` suggested the divergence between the two population is
deeper than the average coalescence within any of the two populations. This
is at odds with the analyses in `2025-07-09`, where we prove that the effective
number of *different* populations was not much larger than 1.0. The previous
`bpp` results also contrast with SNAPPER's analysis, run by Mar either including
or excluding the admixed individuals.

The main difference between the `bpp` execution and previous results is that
`bpp` was run in `2025-11-06` on the sequences found in `2023-05-17b/crepi95_outfiles/crepi95.alleles`,
which is one of the output files from `ipyrad`. In principle, those sequences
are phased and called with a binomial model that incorporates global allele
frequencies and an estimate of error rates (I think). So, they are not raw
reads, and should not be plagued with sequencing errors. But, still, they were
obtained by `ipyrad` with low coverage data. Chances are that they are less
accurate than the genotypes called by ANGSD in `2025-03-15`. To rule out the
chance that input data biased `bpp`'s result in `2025-06-11`, I will run it
again with diploid sequences (instead of haplotypes) derived from the genotypes
called with ANGSD in `2025-03-15`.

## Preparation of data files

In `2025-03-15` we have the following files:

- `toRad.geno`: genotype matrix of RAD loci in 96 samples, coded as *minor* allele
  count (0, 1 or 2), with the value -1 for missing data.
- `toRef.geno`: genotype matrix of reference-mapped loci in 96 samples.
- `toRad.mafs.gz`: compressed list of RAD loci specifying the alleles present and
  which one is considered the minor one.
- `toRef.mafs.gz`: same, for reference-mapped loci.
- `bamlist1.txt`: list of BAM files mapped to the reference genome.
- `bamlist2.txt`: list of BAM files mapped to the RAD loci.

We should also take into account the analyisis in `2025-06-12`, where we found
several loci suspected to be collapsed paralogous regions. To filter them out,
a HWE test was run individually in each population. The inbreeding coefficient
*F* reported in the `.hwe.gz` files was used to remove sites where all samples
were heterozygous ($F \simeq -1$). I can use those reports, but the goal is to
filter full loci, not individual sites, because collapsed paralogy, if real,
must be a problem of the whole locus.

### Collapsed paralogous loci revisited

```{bash}
# These are needed to remove collapsed paralogous loci:
if [ ! -e toRef.far.hwe ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-06-12/ref/SFS/unfiltered/farionis.hwe.gz > toRef.far.hwe
fi

if [ ! -e toRef.pse.hwe ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-06-12/ref/SFS/unfiltered/pseudofarionis.hwe.gz > toRef.pse.hwe
fi

if [ ! -e toRad.far.hwe ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-06-12/rad/SFS/unfiltered/farionis.hwe.gz > toRad.far.hwe
fi

if [ ! -e toRad.pse.hwe ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-06-12/rad/SFS/unfiltered/pseudofarionis.hwe.gz > toRad.pse.hwe
fi
```

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=10, echo=FALSE}
RadFarHwe <- read.table('toRad.far.hwe', header = TRUE)
RadPseHwe <- read.table('toRad.pse.hwe', header = TRUE)
RefFarHwe <- read.table('toRef.far.hwe', header = TRUE)
RefPseHwe <- read.table('toRef.pse.hwe', header = TRUE)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(c(0, 0.5), c(-1, 1), type = 'n', main = 'RAD loci, C. farionis',
     xlab = 'Minor allele frequency', ylab = 'Inbreeding coefficient')
f <- sample(1:nrow(RadFarHwe), 10000)
points(RadFarHwe[f, 'Freq'], RadFarHwe[f, 'F'], pch = 16, cex = 0.5)

plot(c(0, 0.5), c(-1, 1), type = 'n', main = 'RAD loci, C. pseudofarionis',
     xlab = 'Minor allele frequency', ylab = 'Inbreeding coefficient')
f <- sample(1:nrow(RadPseHwe), 10000)
points(RadPseHwe[f, 'Freq'], RadPseHwe[f, 'F'], pch = 16, cex = 0.5)

plot(c(0, 0.5), c(-1, 1), type = 'n', main = 'Reference loci, C. farionis',
     xlab = 'Minor allele frequency', ylab = 'Inbreeding coefficient')
f <- sample(1:nrow(RefFarHwe), 10000)
points(RefFarHwe[f, 'Freq'], RefFarHwe[f, 'F'], pch = 16, cex = 0.5)

plot(c(0, 0.5), c(-1, 1), type = 'n', main = 'Reference loci, C. pseudofarionis',
     xlab = 'Minor allele frequency', ylab = 'Inbreeding coefficient')
f <- sample(1:nrow(RefPseHwe), 10000)
points(RefPseHwe[f, 'Freq'], RefPseHwe[f, 'F'], pch = 16, cex = 0.5)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

I do not think there is any biological reason for such a relationship between
allele frequency and deviation from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium. Because both
parameters were estimated jointly by maximum likelihood with ANGSD, I assume
the relationship is an artifact of the method, maybe due to very low coverage.
In any case, high MAF sites are a minority. We may not loose much by removing
RAD loci containing sites with very negative inbreeding coefficients. The main
discontinuity in the ECDF of the minimum *F* value per locus is at the the
lowest value, which justifies using the same threshold as in `2025-06-12`.

### Filtering of RAD loci

```{r}
suppressMessages(library('dplyr'))
RadFarSum <- summarise(
   RadFarHwe,
   .by = Chromo,
   MinF   = min(F)
)

RadPseSum <- summarise(
   RadPseHwe,
   .by = Chromo,
   MinF   = min(F)
)

plot(ecdf(RadFarSum$MinF), main = c('Lowest F per locus'))
lines(ecdf(RadPseSum$MinF), col = 'blue')
legend(0.4, 0.4, c('C. farionis', 'C. pseudofarionis'),
                   lwd = 2, col = c('black', 'blue'), bty = 'n')

SelectedRadLoci <- intersect(
   RadFarSum[RadFarSum$MinF > min(RadFarSum$MinF), 'Chromo'],
   RadPseSum[RadPseSum$MinF > min(RadPseSum$MinF), 'Chromo'])

write(SelectedRadLoci, 'SelectedRadLoci.txt')
```

Following the estrategy in `2025-03-15`, I subdivide reference contigs by
loci, but I set the maximum gap length to only 100 (it was 1000 before).
That is, contiguous sites are the same locus, long as it may be. And when
a site with genotype data is more than 100 bases from the previous site
with data, it becomes a new locus. I define loci within the `2025-03-15/toRef.geno`
file, which has the same coordinates as `2025-03-15/toRef.mafs.gz`, and holds
data from the two populations. However, the coordinates are different in
`toRef.far.hwe` and `toRef.pse.hwe`, which hold the HWE information required
to filter loci. It was difficult to transfer the locus information from
the *geno* file to the *hwe*s within R. When using coordinates of a *hwe*
file as indices of the *geno* file, the assignment of locus values would neither
fail nor finish, because R got stuck with non-existent indices. The way I do
it below is to reduce the *hwe* files to only positions present in the *geno*
file. Only then the assignment of values works fine.

### Filtering of loci mapped to the reference genome

```{r, eval=TRUE}
MaxDist <- 100
toRef.sample <- sub('.bam', '', basename(
  scan('../2025-03-15/bamlist1.txt',
       what = 'character', quiet = TRUE)))
GenoRef <- read.table('../2025-03-15/toRef.geno',
                      col.names = c('Contig', 'Pos', toRef.sample))
Map <- GenoRef[, c('Contig', 'Pos')]
n <- nrow(Map)
Map$Dist <- c(NA, Map[2:n, 'Pos'] - Map[1:(n - 1), 'Pos'])
previousContig <- c('NullContig',  Map[1:(n - 1), 'Contig'])
Map[Map$Chromo != previousContig, 'Dist'] <- NA
Map$Locus <- cumsum(is.na(Map$Dist) | Map$Dist > MaxDist)
row.names(Map) <- paste(Map$Contig, Map$Pos, sep = ':')

GenoRef$Locus <- Map$Locus

RFH <- RefFarHwe[paste(RefFarHwe$Chromo, RefFarHwe$Position, sep = ':') %in%
                    row.names(Map), ]
RFH$Locus <- Map[paste(RFH$Chromo,
                       RFH$Position,
                       sep = ':'), 'Locus']

RPH <- RefPseHwe[paste(RefPseHwe$Chromo, RefPseHwe$Position, sep = ':') %in%
                    row.names(Map), ]
RPH$Locus <- Map[paste(RPH$Chromo,
                       RPH$Position,
                       sep = ':'), 'Locus']

RefFarSum <- summarise(
   RFH,
   .by = Locus,
   MinF   = min(F)
)
RefPseSum <- summarise(
   RPH,
   .by = Locus,
   MinF   = min(F)
)
MapSum <- dplyr::summarise(Map, .by = Locus,
                    Contig = dplyr::first(Contig),
                    Start  = min(Pos),
                    End    = max(Pos))
write.table(MapSum, file = 'RefLoci.txt', quote = FALSE,
            sep = '\t', row.names = FALSE)

SelectedRefLoci <- intersect(
   RefFarSum[RefFarSum$MinF > min(RefFarSum$MinF), 'Locus'],
   RefPseSum[RefPseSum$MinF > min(RefPseSum$MinF), 'Locus']
)
```

Only `r length(SelectedRefLoci)` are devoid of sites where all samples
seem heterozygous in both populations.

### Reconstruction of loci alignments
Recall that sequences used in SNAPPER were obtained by calling genotypes
with ANGSD based on their posterior probabilities (`2025-03-15`). We used
the `-doGeno 2` flag in ANGSD, which produces genotypes coded by count of
the minor allele (0, 1, 2) or -1 if the genotype is not called. Those
genotypes are in `2025-03-15/toRad.geno` and `2025-03-15/toRef.geno`. The
corresponding minor and major alleles are in `2025-03-15/to*.mafs` files.
The heterozygous positions should be turned to ambiguous IUPAC nucleotide
codes (I think). The `bpp` program will use ambiguity codes if `cleandata = 0`
is in order.

```{bash}
if [ ! -e toRef.mafs ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-03-15/toRef.mafs.gz > toRef.mafs
fi
if [ ! -e toRad.mafs ]; then
   gunzip -c ../2025-03-15/toRad.mafs.gz > toRad.mafs
fi
```

```{r, eval=TRUE}
devnull <- sapply(c('RadFarHwe', 'RadPseHwe', 'RefFarHwe', 'RefPseHwe',
                    'RadFarSum', 'RadPseSum', 'RefFarSum', 'RefPseSum'),
                  function(x) if (x %in% ls()) rm(x))

toRad.sample <- sub('.bam', '', basename(
  scan('../2025-03-15/bamlist2.txt',
       what = 'character', quiet = TRUE)))
all.equal(toRef.sample, toRad.sample)

MafsRef <- read.table('toRef.mafs', header = TRUE)
stopifnot(all.equal(GenoRef$Contig, MafsRef$chromo))
stopifnot(all.equal(GenoRef$Pos,    MafsRef$position))
MafsRef$Locus <- Map$Locus
GenoRef <- GenoRef[GenoRef$Locus %in% SelectedRefLoci, ]

GenoRad <- read.table('../2025-03-15/toRad.geno',
                      col.names = c('Locus', 'Pos', toRad.sample))
GenoRad <- GenoRad[GenoRad$Locus %in% SelectedRadLoci, ]
MafsRad <- read.table('toRad.mafs', header = TRUE)

GeneticIds <- read.table('../2024-10-05/summary.txt', header = TRUE)
GeneticIds$species <- ifelse(GeneticIds$K2.1 > 0.95, 'pseudofarionis', 'unknown')
GeneticIds$species <- ifelse(GeneticIds$K2.2 > 0.95, 'farionis', GeneticIds$species)
farionis <- GeneticIds[GeneticIds$species == 'farionis',       'Sample']
pseudofa <- GeneticIds[GeneticIds$species == 'pseudofarionis', 'Sample']
minCount2Seq <- function(x, minor, major){
   # Intended to turn one vector of minor counts (for one locus)
   # into a string of nucleotides, knowning the minor and major
   # alleles at those sites.
   stopifnot(is.numeric(x))
   stopifnot(all(x >= -1))
   stopifnot(all(x <= 2))
   stopifnot(length(x) == length(minor))
   stopifnot(length(minor) == length(major))
   x <- x + 2
   hets <- Biostrings::mergeIUPACLetters(paste0(minor, major))
   Code <- cbind(rep('-', length(x)), major, hets, minor)
   Seq <- paste0(mapply(function(i, j) Code[i, j], 1:length(x), x),
                 collapse = '')
   return(Seq)
}

if (! file.exists('crepiRad.phy')) {
   phyfile = file('crepiRad.phy', 'w')
   devnull <- lapply(
      SelectedRadLoci,
      function(x) {
         Minor <- MafsRad[MafsRad$chromo == x, 'minor']
         Major <- MafsRad[MafsRad$chromo == x, 'major']
         Genos <- GenoRad[GenoRad$Locus == x, ]
         if (length(Minor) > 25) {
            Seqs <- lapply(
               toRad.sample,
               function(y) {
                  s <- minCount2Seq(Genos[, y], Minor, Major)
                  if (stringr::str_count(s, '-') < 0.25 * nchar(s)) {
                     return(s)
                  } else {
                     return(NULL)
                  }
               }
            )
            names(Seqs) <- toRad.sample
            Seqs <- Seqs[! sapply(Seqs, is.null)]
            NumFar <- sum(names(Seqs) %in% farionis)
            NumPse <- sum(names(Seqs) %in% pseudofa)
            if ((NumFar > 1) & (NumPse > 1)) {
               Seqs <- Seqs[names(Seqs) %in% c(farionis, pseudofa)]
               cat(paste0(length(Seqs), ' ', length(Minor), '\n'),
                   file = phyfile, append = TRUE)
               for (i in 1:length(Seqs)) {
                  cat(paste0(x, '^', names(Seqs)[i], '   ', Seqs[i], '\n'),
                      file = phyfile, append = TRUE)
               }
            }
         }
      })
   close(phyfile)
}

if (! file.exists('crepiRef.phy')) {
   phyfile = file('crepiRef.phy', 'w')
   devnull <- lapply(
      SelectedRefLoci,
      function(x) {
         Minor <- MafsRef[MafsRef$Locus == x, 'minor']
         Major <- MafsRef[MafsRef$Locus == x, 'major']
         Genos <- GenoRef[GenoRef$Locus == x, ]
         if (length(Minor) > 25) {
            Seqs <- lapply(
               toRef.sample,
               function(y) {
                  s <- minCount2Seq(Genos[, y], Minor, Major)
                  if (stringr::str_count(s, '-') < 0.25 * nchar(s)) {
                     return(s)
                  } else {
                     return(NULL)
                  }
               }
            )
            names(Seqs) <- toRef.sample
            Seqs <- Seqs[! sapply(Seqs, is.null)]
            NumFar <- sum(names(Seqs) %in% farionis)
            NumPse <- sum(names(Seqs) %in% pseudofa)
            if ((NumFar > 1) & (NumPse > 1)) {
               Seqs <- Seqs[names(Seqs) %in% c(farionis, pseudofa)]
               cat(paste0(length(Seqs), ' ', length(Minor), '\n'),
                   file = phyfile, append = TRUE)
               for (i in 1:length(Seqs)) {
                  cat(paste0(x, '^', names(Seqs)[i], '   ', Seqs[i], '\n'),
                      file = phyfile, append = TRUE)
               }
            }
         }
      })
   close(phyfile)
}
```

## Running `bpp`
The `bpp` will not be able to use loci with too many samples or with too many
variable sites, because now we are using diploid sequences, which need to be
phased, and `bpp` considers every possible combination of alleles along
heterozygous sites of a locus. Before preparing the control files, I need to
reduce the data set and select up to 7 sequences per population.

Loci have in general unexpectedly high average fraction of heterozygous sites
per sequence (not shown). I apply some arbitrary filter for excess of heterozygosity
just to facilitate `bpp`'s job. Inevitably, this introduces a bias: we will
estimate population parameters from sites chosen to be less variable.

Below I use the functions `rand()` and `asorti()` in `gawk` to randomly
choose a few sequences from each population. The dataset from alignments to
the reference does not seem good enough. From RAD loci I generate a third
data file with up to 4 sequences per population and including 2, 3 or 4
sequences from lake Bienne, which are suspected to be *C. metoecus*.

### Data file reduction

```{bash}
# "A" is C. farionis, "B" is C. pseudofarionis and C...
if [ ! -e imap.txt ]; then
   tail -n +2 ../2024-10-05/summary.txt | \
   gawk '($3 > 0.95){
      print $1 "\tA"
   }($2 > 0.95){
      print $1 "\tB"
   }' > imap.txt
   echo -e "N044Cx2\tC" >> imap.txt
   echo -e "N048Cma\tC" >> imap.txt
   echo -e "N048Cmb\tC" >> imap.txt
   echo -e "N048Cmc\tC" >> imap.txt
fi

if [ ! -e crepiRad2.phy ]; then
   gawk -v MAXHET=3 '(FILENAME == "imap.txt"){
      SP[$1] = $2
   }(/\^/){
      split($1, A, /\^/)
      LOC = A[1]
      SMP = A[2]
      SEQ[A[2]] = $2
      HET = gsub(/[YRMKSW]/, "n", $2)
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "A")) {
         NUMA += 1
         ORDA[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDA, NEWA)
      }
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "B")) {
         NUMB += 1
         ORDB[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDB, NEWB)
      }
      if (HET == MAXHET) WARN++ 
   }(/^[0-9]+ [0-9]+$/){
      if ((NUMA >= 7) && (NUMB >= 7) && (WARN < 4)) {
         print "14 " length(SEQ[SMP])
         for (i = 1; i <= 7; i++) {
            SA = ORDA[NEWA[i]]
            SB = ORDB[NEWB[i]]
            print LOC "^" SA "   " SEQ[SA]
            print LOC "^" SB "   " SEQ[SB]
         }
      }
      delete SEQ
      delete ORDA
      delete ORDB
      delete NEWA
      delete NEWB
      NUMA = 0
      NUMB = 0
      WARN = 0
   }' imap.txt crepiRad.phy > crepiRad2.phy
fi

if [ ! -e crepiRef2.phy ]; then
   gawk -v MAXHET=4 '(FILENAME == "imap.txt"){
      SP[$1] = $2
   }(/\^/){
      split($1, A, /\^/)
      LOC = A[1]
      SMP = A[2]
      SEQ[A[2]] = $2
      HET = gsub(/[YRMKSW]/, "n", $2)
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "A")) {
         NUMA += 1
         ORDA[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDA, NEWA)
      }
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "B")) {
         NUMB += 1
         ORDB[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDB, NEWB)
      }
      if (HET == MAXHET) WARN++ 
   }(/^[0-9]+ [0-9]+$/){
      if ((NUMA >= 7) && (NUMB >= 7) && (WARN < 5)) {
         print "14 " length(SEQ[SMP])
         for (i = 1; i <= 7; i++) {
            SA = ORDA[NEWA[i]]
            SB = ORDB[NEWB[i]]
            print LOC "^" SA "   " SEQ[SA]
            print LOC "^" SB "   " SEQ[SB]
         }
      }
      delete SEQ
      delete ORDA
      delete ORDB
      delete NEWA
      delete NEWB
      NUMA = 0
      NUMB = 0
      WARN = 0
   }' imap.txt crepiRef.phy > crepiRef2.phy
fi

if [ ! -e crepiRad3.phy ]; then
   gawk -v MAXHET=3 '(FILENAME == "imap.txt"){
      SP[$1] = $2
   }(/\^/){
      split($1, A, /\^/)
      LOC = A[1]
      SMP = A[2]
      SEQ[A[2]] = $2
      HET = gsub(/[YRMKSW]/, "n", $2)
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "A")) {
         NUMA += 1
         ORDA[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDA, NEWA)
      }
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "B")) {
         NUMB += 1
         ORDB[sprintf("%.0f", rand() * 10000)] = A[2]
         asorti(ORDB, NEWB)
      }
      if ((HET <= MAXHET) && (SP[SMP] == "C")) {
         NUMC += 1
         ORDC[NUMC] = A[2]
      }
      if (HET == MAXHET) WARN++ 
   }(/^[0-9]+ [0-9]+$/){
      if ((NUMA >= 4) && (NUMB >= 4) && (NUMC > 1) && (WARN < 10)) {
         print 4 + 4 + NUMC " " length(SEQ[SMP])
         for (i = 1; i <= 4; i++) {
            SA = ORDA[NEWA[i]]
            SB = ORDB[NEWB[i]]
            print LOC "^" SA "   " SEQ[SA]
            print LOC "^" SB "   " SEQ[SB]
         }
         for (i in ORDC) {
            print LOC "^" ORDC[i] "   " SEQ[ORDC[i]]
         }
      }
      delete SEQ
      delete ORDA
      delete ORDB
      delete ORDC
      delete NEWA
      delete NEWB
      delete NEWC
      NUMA = 0
      NUMB = 0
      NUMC = 0
      WARN = 0
   }' imap.txt crepiRad.phy > crepiRad3.phy
fi
```

### One species

```{bash}
if [ ! -e template.ctl ]; then
   echo "seed = -1"                                > template.ctl
   echo "seqfile = input.phy"                     >> template.ctl
   echo "Imapfile = imap.txt"                     >> template.ctl
   echo "jobname = out.txt"                       >> template.ctl
   echo "speciesdelimitation = 0"                 >> template.ctl
   echo "speciestree = 0"                         >> template.ctl
   echo "species&tree = 2 A B"                    >> template.ctl
   echo "                 7 7  * maxseqs"         >> template.ctl
   echo "               (A,B); * guidetree"       >> template.ctl
   echo "phase = 1 1"                             >> template.ctl
   echo "usedata = 1"                             >> template.ctl
   echo "nloci = 1000"                            >> template.ctl
   echo "alphaprior = 1 1 4"                      >> template.ctl
   echo "cleandata = 0"                           >> template.ctl
   echo "thetaprior = 3 0.04 e"                   >> template.ctl
   echo "tauprior = 3 0.01"                       >> template.ctl
   echo "locusrate = 1 0 0 5.0 iid"               >> template.ctl
   echo "clock = 1"                               >> template.ctl
   echo "finetune = 1"                            >> template.ctl
   echo "print = 1 0 0 0 0"                       >> template.ctl
   echo "burnin = 25000"                          >> template.ctl
   echo "sampfreq = 250"                          >> template.ctl
   echo "nsample = 100000"                        >> template.ctl
   echo "threads = 8 25 1"                        >> template.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e onesp1.ctl ]; then
   cp template.ctl onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/Imapfile =/c * Imapfile = imap.txt"   onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/seqfile = /c seqfile = crepiRad2.phy" onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = onesp/out1"    onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/species&tr/c species&tree = 1 A"      onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/ * maxseqs/c            14 * maxseqs" onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/ * guidetr/c               * guidetr" onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/phase = /c phase = 1"                 onesp1.ctl
   sed -i "/finetune =/c finetune = 1 Gage:99.000000 Gspr:0.001216 th1:0.000382 tau:0.000000 mix:0.041259 alfa:2.638333 mu_i:0.867624" onesp1.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e onesp2.ctl ]; then
   cp onesp1.ctl onesp2.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = onesp/out2"    onesp2.ctl
   sed -i "/threads = /c threads = 8 17 1"        onesp2.ctl
fi

if [ ! -d onesp ]; then mkdir onesp; fi
if [ ! -e onesp/out1.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile onesp1.ctl 1> onesp/out1.log 2> onesp/out1.err &
fi
if [ ! -e onesp/out2.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile onesp2.ctl 1> onesp/out2.log 2> onesp/out2.err &
fi
wait
```

### Two isolated species

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
if [ ! -e imap2.txt ]; then
   grep -v -P "\tC$" imap.txt > imap2.txt
fi
if [ ! -d twosp ]; then mkdir twosp; fi
if [ ! -e twosp1.ctl ]; then
   cp template.ctl twosp1.ctl
   sed -i "/seqfile = /c seqfile = crepiRad2.phy"    twosp1.ctl
   sed -i "/Imapfile =/c Imapfile = imap2.txt"       twosp1.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = twosp/out1"       twosp1.ctl
   sed -i "/finetune =/c finetune = 1" twosp1.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e twosp2.ctl ]; then
   cp twosp1.ctl twosp2.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = twosp/out2"       twosp2.ctl
   sed -i "/threads = /c threads = 8 17 1"           twosp2.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e twosp/out1.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile twosp1.ctl 1> twosp/out1.log 2> twosp/out1.err &
fi

if [ ! -e twosp/out2.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile twosp2.ctl 1> twosp/out2.log 2> twosp/out2.err &
fi
wait
```

### Three isolated species

   sed -i "/ * maxseqs/c                  4 4 4"      threesp1.ctl

### Two species with migration

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
if [ ! -d twoMig ]; then mkdir twoMig; fi
if [ ! -e twoMig1.ctl ]; then
   cp template.ctl twoMig1.ctl
   sed -i "/seqfile = /c seqfile = crepiRad2.phy"    twoMig1.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = twoMig/out1"      twoMig1.ctl
   sed -i "/phase = /c *newline  \nphase = 1 1"      twoMig1.ctl
   sed -i "/*newline /c migprior = 2 200\n*newline " twoMig1.ctl
   sed -i "/*newline /c migration 2\n  A B\n  B A"   twoMig1.ctl
fi
if [ ! -e twoMig2.ctl ]; then
   cp twoMig1.ctl twoMig2.ctl
   sed -i "/jobname = /c jobname = twoMig/out2"      twoMig2.ctl
   sed -i "/threads = /c threads = 8 17 1"           twoMig2.ctl
fi

if [ ! -e twoMig/out1.txt ]; then

fi
if [ ! -e twoMig/out2.txt ]; then
   bpp --cfile twoMig2.ctl 1> twoMig/out2.log 2> twoMig/out2.err &
fi
wait
```

## Analysis of results

### One species

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
source('mcmc.R')
mcmc1 <- read.table('onesp/out1.mcmc.txt', header = TRUE)
mcmc2 <- read.table('onesp/out2.mcmc.txt', header = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
autocorPlot(mcmc1)
autocorPlot(mcmc2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r, fig.width=4, fig.height=8}
tendencyPlot(mcmc1)
tendencyPlot(mcmc2)

convergencePlot(mcmc1, mcmc2)
```

```{r}
onesp <- rbind(mcmc1, mcmc2)
plot(density(onesp$theta.1.A, bw = 'SJ'), main = expression(theta[A]))
abline(v = mean(onesp$theta.1.A), col = 'red', lty = 2)
text(0.015, 1000, sprintf("Mean = %.4f\nS.D. = %.4f",
                           mean(onesp$theta.1.A),
                           sd(onesp$theta.1.A)))
```
